PETROL DEPOT HEIST

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Criminals have moved on from petrol tanker hijackings to petrol depot heists - maximising underworld profit by cleaning out an entire depot.

Summary:
Earlier this year we covered a story on petrol tankers being hijacked on freeways while on route to make deliveries, but it seems that criminals have upped their game. They've gone one link up in the petrol industry chain. Rather than taking the risk of hijacking a single tanker at a time. These criminals now target an entire depot! They bring their own tankers and take every single drop of fuel. We have CCTV footage of one of these depot heists. Carte Blanche investigates.

Further information:
I have CCTV footage of a heist in May. Subsequently the owner, an ex-cop, tracked down the stolen petrol by following a trail of spilt fuel. Arrests were made. The man behind it is William - he runs a "logistics" company and owns trucks used in these heists.
The depot heists calmed down while William was in jail. But as soon as he was released a few weeks ago, the action picked up again. Another depot knocked in Alrode.
I have a case going back to January - same MO and William is mentioned in the statements.

We expose a new type of criminal MO and connect the dots back to a known suspect that was in police custody but released again.

INTERVIEWS -
- ACTION FUELS - CCTV FOOTAGE OF HEIST
- BAKERS TRANSPORT - MOST RECENT HEIST
- SEBOKENG FUELS - JANUARY CASE
- INFORMANT THAT WORKED WITH WILLIAM ON THE JANUARY CASE
- FUEL INDUSTRY EXPERT ABOUT THE INCREASE IN THESE TYPES OF HEISTS
- PAUL RAMALOKO - HAWKS

Press Release:


Petrol Depot Heists
Why hijack only a fuel tanker when you can rob an entire depot? Petrol thieves have upped their game, cleaning out entire depots with military precision and earning themselves millions selling the liquid gold on the black market. Carte Blanche follows their trail.


Script:


PETROL DEPOT HEISTS

PETER: It’s worth so much, it’s easy to sell and you can never trace it. It’s not a crime of opportunity – it’s very, very carefully planned.

VO: It’s been called liquid gold. Bulk fuel theft is costing the country millions of rands - bordering on economic sabotage.

LINK: Criminals have upped their game and are moving on from high- risk petrol tanker hijackings to petrol depot heists – making off with even bigger bounties.

VO: Brazen robbers arrive with their own trucks at petrol depots, taking over the yard at gunpoint and stealing every drop of fuel they can load – often making off with hundreds of thousands of rands worth in just one hit.

Their MO is simple - criminals often spread their dodgy operations far and wide to avoid detection says Pine Pienaar from The South African Insurance Crime Bureau.

PINE: What we’ve picked up is that they usually hit smaller depots in small rural areas //and then it wouldn’t receive a lot of attention // so you wouldn’t link the cases together

VO: Every day can feel like a Sunday in some small towns around South Africa. But don’t be fooled, these small towns are becoming prime targets for criminals, where small independent fuel depots are being turned into crime scenes.

Two weeks ago, Bethal in Mpumalanga was hit by robbers who were caught red-handed stealing fuel at Vecto Petroleum.

Pine was on the scene that night.

PINE: The pump was on the wall connected the one end to the depot’s reserve tank here and the other one to their own fuel tanker and they were in this process of starting to pump over diesel.

DEVI: So they knew what they were doing?
PINE: they knew what they were doing – you could see that they had done it before.

VO: The two men caught in the act were arrested for armed robbery.

They told Pine they were employed by a man called Percy. He owns Icon Logistics Services in Vereeniging nearly 200 km away.

LINK: The owner Percy Makwetlane declined to be interviewed, but denied the allegations in a phone conversation.

UPSOUND: I don’t know anything about the diesel robberies. I didn’t send the driver to go do the robbery.

VO: This Mercedes Benz truck is registered to Percy’s company and was recovered in the Bethal robbery. It has been impounded by the police. Subsequently, it has been reported stolen.

In June this year, in Meyerton a similar white Mercedes Benz Truck was involved in a robbery at Action Fuels. Armed robbers took over the depot.
.
This CCTV footage shows the robbers getting aggressive with the yard workers. Ex-cop Pieter Hamman owns Action Fuels.

PIETER: They went to our storage tanks – break it open and they empty all of our storage tanks – 90 000 litres.
DEVI: What was the value of the fuel you lost?
PIETER: The fuel was R1.1 million – then all the damage to the paving, they took equipment, stepladder, toolboxes, everthing they could load on top of the truck they took – all of that added up to an amount of R1.5 million.

VO: But this time, the robbers unwittingly left a clue.

PIETER: They overfilled the trucks in such a way that they overspill – so as they go onto the freeway there was a diesel trial that I followed

VO: Not a stranger to investigations, Pieter traced the diesel trail to an address in Vereeniging - interestingly, this property is also linked to ICON LOGISTICS Services, the company implicated in the Bethal robbery.

Sadly for Pieter, there was no sign of the trucks that stole his diesel.

But the next day, one of the robbers’ trucks was spotted at the truck stop opposite Natref in Sasolburg.

Pieter recovered a load of fuel, but even better, he was able to identify the truck owners.

PIETER: We see it’s Forex Logistics, we traced it back to this address and then puzzles fall in to place. When we came on Monday afternoon, the other truck was here.

VO: Both of the trucks involved in the Action Fuels robbery in June were confiscated by police.

LINK: It appears that Petrol Depot Robbers are not only brazen, they are also professionals – they know the fuel industry, often running their own transport companies.

VO: Fuel industry representative, Peter Morgan, believes this kind of crime cripples the economy.

PETER: Whoever is doing it knows the industry quite intimately – it’s somebody who knows how the industry operates – it’s not a complete stranger. INT 1 M9

VO: This man, William Macholo, Operational Manager for Forex Logistics and Petroleum, handed himself over to police after the Action Fuels robbery.

Willam was later released on R20 000 bail claiming the company’s trucks had been hired out to an Isaac Msiza from TMRN Construction when the robbery occurred.

We tracked down the only director of the company

LINK: We’re in Bophelong and we’re looking for Thabo Dube, the address we have for him is 65 B Mofolo Street – let’s see if he’s home?

DEVI: Looking for Thabo Dube?
RESIDENT: He doesn’t live here any more
DEVI: Is he gone?
RESIDENT: YEs

VO: We called Thabo.

DEVI: Do you know William Macholo
THABO: No Ma’am //
DEVI: He rented to Izak Maziza and he runs TMRN – but TMRN is your company?
THABO: Yes, it is my company – not Izak Maziza // I don't know Izak Maziza. That TMRN – I opened it for construction – so , I never did a job on anything – I am not working on fuels and stuff.

VO: Thabo confirmed this in an official statement to the police.

We compared notes with PI Danie Day - who specializes in bulk theft investigations.

Since October last year, he has investigated three depot heists - two of the cases involved a White Merecedes Benz Truck similar to the one used at Vecto Petroleum in Bethal and Action Fuels in Meyerton.

DEVI: If it’s the same MO, can you say it’s the same syndicate?
DANIE: You can’t – but in this instance we do agree that it might be the same syndicate for the simple reason it is the same modus operandi

VO: Danie says the fact that similar trucks were used could also point to this being the same syndicate. But we were able to make another connection to Danie’s case at Sebokeng Fuels in Rustenburg, in January this year.

The then yard supervisor was in on the job and helped robbers get away with 90 000 litres of diesel valued at R980 000.

DANIE: He was paid R75 000 –
DEVI: That’s a big tip
DANIE: 99% of theft at the diesel depot is inside – for the simple reason –//they are less exposed // they load and then they go

VO: The yard supervisor later turned on his accomplices, outing the man in charge of the robbery as someone called “William”

DANIE: William is the guy that actually went there with the two trucks, he loaded the load and he paid the guy, he handed the money over.

VO: While the Sebokeng Fuels robber may not be the same William linked to the Action Fuels robbery, police are investigating this link.

LINK: The problem with this investigation is that these robberies are treated as individual cases - despite the glaring similarities police have yet to connect the dots

VO: We managed to find yet another case involving a Mercedes-Benz Truck.

West Rand Transport Company, PAYLOADS, was hit by armed petrol depot robbers in March this year.

This CCTV footage shows the robbers arriving. They used two Merecedes Benz trucks and a third Nissan UD 40 that night. Operational director Daan Joubert JR, says the guard mistook them for a legit company.

DAAN: They got out of their vehicles, they were armed – there were some trucks standing over in the yard as well, the drivers were sleeping in their cabs - they forced the guys out of their trucks and tied them up in our security office.

VO: With free reign of the yard – the crooks offloaded three of Payloads’ petrol tankers – that’s R1.5 million rands worth of fuel in just five hours.

DEVI: Did the robbers come across as if they knew what they were doing?
DAAN: it’s not petty criminals – this was organized, they knew what they were coming from, they knew exactly how much.

VO: To date no arrests have been made on this case.

Pine Pienaar says these criminals go to a lot of trouble to operate under the radar.

PINE: They would drive // using back roads, they don't go on to tolls roads or anything //They would sometimes use // overalls – so that when you pass by – the casual eye, it will just look like it’s normal business.

VO: Despite providing Hawks Spokesperson, Paul Ramaloko with case numbers he was unable to comment on specific incidents.

PAUL: we would not want to name indiviuals, we know the big faces, those that are not already behind bars – we don’t want alert them that we are coming we doing lot work around the syndicates

VO: Pieter doesn’t have much confidence in the police at this stage

PIETER: They phone me every once or twice a week asking for new information – so I give them information, but nothing’s happened.

VO: We wanted to speak to William from Forex Logistics and Petroleum, who is facing charges in connection with the Action Fuels robbery. We traced him to this address in Sasolburg.

UPSOUND: William’s not here.

VO: With no sign of him at the company’s Vereeniging Premises either, we called him. He agreed to meet us.

UPSOUND: I’ll see you there at the Spar.

VO: We drove a 100km to Koppies in the Northern Free State, but William was nowhere to be found.

He later referred us to an Advocate Monareng.

UPSOUND: Will comment in court as the case is still pending.

VO: And until then, there’s not much else to do says PI Danie Day.

DANIE: sadly we can only take it that far, we can identify the suspects or arrest them but once it’s in the hands of the police or the courts we cannot really take it much further.

VO: Despite the links between the different cases - no further arrests have been made.

PROMO 1
VO: Fuel is liquid gold. In high demand it brings in big bucks on the black market. We expose a new MO – Petrol Depot Heists.

DAAN: it’s not petty criminals – this was organized, they knew what they were coming from, they knew exactly how much.

PROMO 2
VO: Petrol theft syndicates have upped their game. Entire petrol depots are hit with military precision with losses running into the millions.

PETER: Whoever is doing it knows the industry quite intimately – it’s somebody who knows how the industry operates – it’s not a complete stranger.

VO: Carte Blanche investigates

PINE: What we’ve picked up is that they usually hit smaller depots in small rural areas //and then it wouldn’t receive a lot of attention // so you wouldn’t link the cases together VO: Every day can feel like a Sunday in some small towns around South Africa. But don’t be fooled, these small towns are becoming prime targets for criminals, where small independent fuel depots are being turned into crime scenes. Two weeks ago, Bethal in Mpumalanga was hit by robbers who were caught red-handed stealing fuel at Vecto Petroleum. Pine was on the scene that night. PINE: The pump was on the wall connected the one end to the depot’s reserve tank here and the other one to their own fuel tanker and they were in this process of starting to pump over diesel. DEVI: So they knew what they were doing? PINE: they knew what they were doing – you could see that they had done it before. VO: The two men caught in the act were arrested for armed robbery. They told Pine they were employed by a man called Percy. He owns Icon Logistics Services in Vereeniging nearly 200 km away. LINK: The owner Percy Makwetlane declined to be interviewed, but denied the allegations in a phone conversation. UPSOUND: I don’t know anything about the diesel robberies. I didn’t send the driver to go do the robbery. VO: This Mercedes Benz truck is registered to Percy’s company and was recovered in the Bethal robbery. It has been impounded by the police. Subsequently, it has been reported stolen. In June this year, in Meyerton a similar white Mercedes Benz Truck was involved in a robbery at Action Fuels. Armed robbers took over the depot. . This CCTV footage shows the robbers getting aggressive with the yard workers. Ex-cop Pieter Hamman owns Action Fuels. PIETER: They went to our storage tanks – break it open and they empty all of our storage tanks – 90 000 litres. DEVI: What was the value of the fuel you lost? PIETER: The fuel was R1.1 million – then all the damage to the paving, they took equipment, stepladder, toolboxes, everthing they could load on top of the truck they took – all of that added up to an amount of R1.5 million. VO: But this time, the robbers unwittingly left a clue. PIETER: They overfilled the trucks in such a way that they overspill – so as they go onto the freeway there was a diesel trial that I followed VO: Not a stranger to investigations, Pieter traced the diesel trail to an address in Vereeniging - interestingly, this property is also linked to ICON LOGISTICS Services, the company implicated in the Bethal robbery. Sadly for Pieter, there was no sign of the trucks that stole his diesel. But the next day, one of the robbers’ trucks was spotted at the truck stop opposite Natref in Sasolburg. Pieter recovered a load of fuel, but even better, he was able to identify the truck owners. PIETER: We see it’s Forex Logistics, we traced it back to this address and then puzzles fall in to place. When we came on Monday afternoon, the other truck was here. VO: Both of the trucks involved in the Action Fuels robbery in June were confiscated by police. LINK: It appears that Petrol Depot Robbers are not only brazen, they are also professionals – they know the fuel industry, often running their own transport companies. VO: Fuel industry representative, Peter Morgan, believes this kind of crime cripples the economy. PETER: Whoever is doing it knows the industry quite intimately – it’s somebody who knows how the industry operates – it’s not a complete stranger. INT 1 M9 VO: This man, William Macholo, Operational Manager for Forex Logistics and Petroleum, handed himself over to police after the Action Fuels robbery. Willam was later released on R20 000 bail claiming the company’s trucks had been hired out to an Isaac Msiza from TMRN Construction when the robbery occurred. We tracked down the only director of the company LINK: We’re in Bophelong and we’re looking for Thabo Dube, the address we have for him is 65 B Mofolo Street – let’s see if he’s home? DEVI: Looking for Thabo Dube? RESIDENT: He doesn’t live here any more DEVI: Is he gone? RESIDENT: YEs VO: We called Thabo. DEVI: Do you know William Macholo THABO: No Ma’am // DEVI: He rented to Izak Maziza and he runs TMRN – but TMRN is your company? THABO: Yes, it is my company – not Izak Maziza // I don't know Izak Maziza. That TMRN – I opened it for construction – so , I never did a job on anything – I am not working on fuels and stuff. VO: Thabo confirmed this in an official statement to the police. We compared notes with PI Danie Day - who specializes in bulk theft investigations. Since October last year, he has investigated three depot heists - two of the cases involved a White Merecedes Benz Truck similar to the one used at Vecto Petroleum in Bethal and Action Fuels in Meyerton. DEVI: If it’s the same MO, can you say it’s the same syndicate? DANIE: You can’t – but in this instance we do agree that it might be the same syndicate for the simple reason it is the same modus operandi VO: Danie says the fact that similar trucks were used could also point to this being the same syndicate. But we were able to make another connection to Danie’s case at Sebokeng Fuels in Rustenburg, in January this year. The then yard supervisor was in on the job and helped robbers get away with 90 000 litres of diesel valued at R980 000. DANIE: He was paid R75 000 – DEVI: That’s a big tip DANIE: 99% of theft at the diesel depot is inside – for the simple reason –//they are less exposed // they load and then they go VO: The yard supervisor later turned on his accomplices, outing the man in charge of the robbery as someone called “William” DANIE: William is the guy that actually went there with the two trucks, he loaded the load and he paid the guy, he handed the money over. VO: While the Sebokeng Fuels robber may not be the same William linked to the Action Fuels robbery, police are investigating this link. LINK: The problem with this investigation is that these robberies are treated as individual cases - despite the glaring similarities police have yet to connect the dots VO: We managed to find yet another case involving a Mercedes-Benz Truck. West Rand Transport Company, PAYLOADS, was hit by armed petrol depot robbers in March this year. This CCTV footage shows the robbers arriving. They used two Merecedes Benz trucks and a third Nissan UD 40 that night. Operational director Daan Joubert JR, says the guard mistook them for a legit company. DAAN: They got out of their vehicles, they were armed – there were some trucks standing over in the yard as well, the drivers were sleeping in their cabs - they forced the guys out of their trucks and tied them up in our security office. VO: With free reign of the yard – the crooks offloaded three of Payloads’ petrol tankers – that’s R1.5 million rands worth of fuel in just five hours. DEVI: Did the robbers come across as if they knew what they were doing? DAAN: it’s not petty criminals – this was organized, they knew what they were coming from, they knew exactly how much. VO: To date no arrests have been made on this case. Pine Pienaar says these criminals go to a lot of trouble to operate under the radar. PINE: They would drive // using back roads, they don't go on to tolls roads or anything //They would sometimes use // overalls – so that when you pass by – the casual eye, it will just look like it’s normal business. VO: Despite providing Hawks Spokesperson, Paul Ramaloko with case numbers he was unable to comment on specific incidents. PAUL: we would not want to name indiviuals, we know the big faces, those that are not already behind bars – we don’t want alert them that we are coming we doing lot work around the syndicates VO: Pieter doesn’t have much confidence in the police at this stage PIETER: They phone me every once or twice a week asking for new information – so I give them information, but nothing’s happened. VO: We wanted to speak to William from Forex Logistics and Petroleum, who is facing charges in connection with the Action Fuels robbery. We traced him to this address in Sasolburg. UPSOUND: William’s not here. VO: With no sign of him at the company’s Vereeniging Premises either, we called him. He agreed to meet us. UPSOUND: I’ll see you there at the Spar. VO: We drove a 100km to Koppies in the Northern Free State, but William was nowhere to be found. He later referred us to an Advocate Monareng. UPSOUND: Will comment in court as the case is still pending. VO: And until then, there’s not much else to do says PI Danie Day. DANIE: sadly we can only take it that far, we can identify the suspects or arrest them but once it’s in the hands of the police or the courts we cannot really take it much further. VO: Despite the links between the different cases - no further arrests have been made. PROMO 1 VO: Fuel is liquid gold. In high demand it brings in big bucks on the black market. We expose a new MO – Petrol Depot Heists. DAAN: it’s not petty criminals – this was organized, they knew what they were coming from, they knew exactly how much. PROMO 2 VO: Petrol theft syndicates have upped their game. Entire petrol depots are hit with military precision with losses running into the millions. PETER: Whoever is doing it knows the industry quite intimately – it’s somebody who knows how the industry operates – it’s not a complete stranger. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Criminals have moved on from petrol tanker hijackings to petrol depot heists - maximising underworld profit by cleaning out an entire depot.
metadata.Summary: Earlier this year we covered a story on petrol tankers being hijacked on freeways while on route to make deliveries, but it seems that criminals have upped their game. They've gone one link up in the petrol industry chain. Rather than taking the risk of hijacking a single tanker at a time. These criminals now target an entire depot! They bring their own tankers and take every single drop of fuel. We have CCTV footage of one of these depot heists. Carte Blanche investigates.
metadata.Further information: I have CCTV footage of a heist in May. Subsequently the owner, an ex-cop, tracked down the stolen petrol by following a trail of spilt fuel. Arrests were made. The man behind it is William - he runs a "logistics" company and owns trucks used in these heists. The depot heists calmed down while William was in jail. But as soon as he was released a few weeks ago, the action picked up again. Another depot knocked in Alrode. I have a case going back to January - same MO and William is mentioned in the statements. We expose a new type of criminal MO and connect the dots back to a known suspect that was in police custody but released again. INTERVIEWS - - ACTION FUELS - CCTV FOOTAGE OF HEIST - BAKERS TRANSPORT - MOST RECENT HEIST - SEBOKENG FUELS - JANUARY CASE - INFORMANT THAT WORKED WITH WILLIAM ON THE JANUARY CASE - FUEL INDUSTRY EXPERT ABOUT THE INCREASE IN THESE TYPES OF HEISTS - PAUL RAMALOKO - HAWKS
